messages:
Taylor (Customer): Hey, we started getting structured_output parse failures after yesterday's model rollout. Example error from our side: \"SyntaxError: Unexpected token F in JSON at position 124\". Happening when the model returns values like \"id\": \"12345\" (quoted number) and \"active\": \"True\" (capitalized). We're using strict mode and a JSON schema that expects id:number, active:boolean, status: enum [\"active\",\"inactive\"]. Can you advise?

Sam (Support): Sorry about the break — can you paste the exact request and the response body (redact PII)? Also which model and the structured_output mode flag you used?

Taylor (Customer): Sure — here's the curl we used (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACT\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{
    "model":"open-lm-8b",
    "prompt":"generate user record as json",
    "structured_output_mode":"strict",
    "json_schema":{
      "type":"object",
      "properties":{
        "id":{"type":"number"},
        "active":{"type":"boolean"},
        "status":{"type":"string","enum":["active","inactive"]}
      },
      "required":["id","active","status"]
    }
  }'
```

And the failing response body we saw:

```json
{
  "id": "12345",
  "active": "True",
  "status": "ACTIVE"
}
// error: invalid_json_error: JSON.parse failed at position 124
```

Sam (Support): Got it. I can repro locally. Two separate issues here: 1) numeric value returned as a quoted string; 2) boolean returned as capitalized string \"True\" and enum in uppercase. In strict mode we validate that types match exactly and enums match case-sensitive. Workarounds: change schema to accept string OR number for id, or set structured_output_mode to \"lenient\" if available. Quick fix: update schema to:

```json
\"id\": { \"anyOf\": [{\"type\":\"number\"},{\"type\":\"string\"}] }
```

and for enums, either add uppercase variants to enum or post-process to lowercase before validation.

Taylor (Customer): Is this a model regression or a parser change on your side? It started immediately after your 24h model refresh. Also, we got a spike in token usage because our client retried on parse errors — can you help with billing?

Jess (Eng): Looking at the runtime logs — the model occasionally emits booleans as \"True\"/\"False\" (capitalized) and sometimes returns enums in different casing. The strict validator enforces exact JSON parsing. This is not a new parser strictness change; strict mode always validated types, but the v2 model rollout increased the frequency of these casing mismatches.

We have two options: 
- short term: support-side suggestion = change schema to accept both string/number for id and add case-insensitive matching for enums in your client.
- medium term: engineering can add a \"coerce_types\": true option on the structured_output endpoint that will attempt safe coercions (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers, \"True\"/\"False\" -> booleans, case-insensitive enum matching).

Sam (Support): I've filed INC-2026 and pinged eng-oncall for a priority assessment. @Jess can you confirm whether a safe fallback parser is feasible without introducing silent correctness regressions?

eng-oncall: Confirmed — a configurable soft-coerce layer is feasible as a runtime flag; we need to scope tests for edge cases where coercion masks real schema violations. Estimated work: prototype this week, internal rollout next sprint.

Billing Bot: We saw the retries counted as separate requests. If you can share a short window of request ids, we can review for a goodwill credit if it's caused by our model change. Please open a billing ticket referencing INC-2026.

Taylor (Customer): I patched the schema to accept string/number for id and added a small post-validate normalizer to lowercase enums and coerce booleans. That fixed our immediate failures. We'll hold off on retries for 10s until you confirm. Thanks.

Sam (Support): Thanks for confirming the workaround. We'll keep INC-2026 open; Jess will update with timeline for a coerce_types flag. In the meantime, please send billing ticket with sample request_ids and we can evaluate credits. Sorry for the disruption :hugging_face:

Jess (Eng): Following up — plan is to add a non-default \"coerce_types\" flag to the structured output API. No silent coercion in strict mode by default. ETA for PR: 10 days. I'll post the internal RFC link in INC-2026.

Taylor (Customer): Great, appreciated. I'll monitor and re-open if anything else.

Sam (Support): Closing loop here — if you need us to test a staging rollout, we can add you to the early access group.

Taylor (Customer): Please do. Thanks, all! :thumbsup:
